detailed_description:
Angular stylised 3D animation, brush-stroke texture, Surrey, 1894, afternoon sun from the left, black shadows.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:07. The shot opens on a medium shot inside the pit on the glaring afternoon: at the foot of the crusted hull a bare-armed workman in braces drives a spade into the sand, a stout older man in a red waistcoat swings a pickaxe beside him, and a thin grey-haired man in a collarless shirt and a flat cap stoops over a shovel further back; along the rim above them the heads and shoulders of onlookers above the sand edge, each turned a different way: a bald man in shirtsleeves, a woman in a wide black hat, a <Subject 1> on a man's shoulders, two men in dark coats leaning on the edge. The camera is on the pit floor at a standing man's eye, five long strides from the workmen, a 35mm lens. The afternoon sun comes from the LEFT onto the crowd. At the first frame the workmen dig in a row across the BOTTOM third of the frame, their heads a sixth of the frame's height. The dug sand wall rises through the CENTRE. The shot is inside this place: The same great raw crater on Horsell Common on a glaring hot summer afternoon in 1894: the sand walls dug back and scored by spades, planks and pickaxes on the gravel floor, the colossal crusted cylinder thirty yards across lying half-buried, much more of its long hull now uncovered. The camera tilts up from the bare-armed workman's spade in the sand to the heads along the rim as the stout man swings his pickaxe down, from 00:00 to 00:04. At 00:04 one onlooker leans further over the edge, and the lean continues to the last frame of the shot. By 00:07 the camera is tilting up through the last frame, and the action continues with it.
